claims.text: Traditional lightweight metals and standard HEAs generally favor either low density or high strength rather than achieving both simultaneously.
Increasing aluminum content while balancing Ti, Mn, or Cr can induce controlled nanoscale precipitation in an HEA.
The proposed compositional optimization will form nanoscale precipitates within the alloy matrix.
Nanoscale precipitates will strengthen the alloy through precipitation strengthening.
The proposed precipitate-containing matrix will retain a low overall density.
Increasing the optimized aluminum content reduces the alloy's overall density.
Balancing aluminum with selected transition metals promotes nanoscale precipitation.
The nanoscale precipitates enhance strength by impeding dislocation motion.
The optimized aluminum-containing HEA will have lower density than conventional aluminum alloys and traditional HEAs.
The optimized aluminum-containing HEA will have higher tensile strength than conventional aluminum alloys and traditional HEAs.
The optimized aluminum-containing HEA will have better fatigue resistance than conventional aluminum alloys and traditional HEAs.
The optimized aluminum-containing HEA will have better corrosion resistance than conventional aluminum alloys and traditional HEAs.
The anticipated improvements apply under typical service conditions and may differ under extreme or highly aggressive environments.
The magnitude of the mechanical and environmental improvements depends on precise composition and processing conditions.
